title: Philippines Ambassador Invites Indian Travellers, With 14-Day Visa-Free Entry
excerpt: Ambassador Josel F. Ignacio presented honours at the India Travel Awards in New Delhi as Manila courts Indian tourists with visa-free entry and a direct Air India flight.
body:
• Philippine Ambassador to India Josel F. Ignacio presented honours at the India Travel Awards 2026 in New Delhi on October 15 and used the platform to invite Indian travellers to explore the Philippines.
  • Indian passport holders can enter the Philippines visa-free for tourism for up to 14 days, non-extendible, with a passport valid six months beyond the stay, confirmed accommodation, proof of funds and a return or onward ticket.
  • Indians holding a valid US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Schengen or Singapore visa or residence permit qualify for 30 days visa-free; Air India's direct Delhi-Manila flights, five times a week, are the only nonstop link between the two countries.
  • The Philippines is pitching Manila, Cebu, Bohol, Boracay and Palawan to Indian leisure, luxury, honeymoon, MICE and destination-wedding travellers.

The Philippines made its pitch to India's travel trade in person this month. H.E. Josel F. Ignacio, Ambassador of the Philippines to India, presented awards at the India Travel Awards 2026 ceremony in New Delhi on October 15, including the Best Wedding and MICE Hotel honour, and used the occasion to invite Indian travellers to explore the archipelago, according to coverage of the ceremony.

An ambassador on the awards stage

Ignacio presented the award alongside K. B. Kachru, Chairman Emeritus of Radisson Hotel Group, South Asia. His presence at an Indian industry awards night was itself the message: the Philippines wants a larger share of India's outbound market and is courting the trade that sells it. The Philippines Department of Tourism has been running sustained India-focused promotion through its partner Buzz Travel Marketing, including a luxury workshop in New Delhi and, more recently, a nine-day familiarisation trip for five Indian influencers covering Manila, Cebu, Moalboal, Bohol and Batangas, Trav Talk reported.

That itinerary shows what Manila is selling: city heritage in Intramuros and San Agustin Church in Manila, canyoneering at Kawasan Falls, the sardine run in Moalboal, the Chocolate Hills and Tarsier Sanctuary in Bohol, and wellness stays such as The Farm at San Benito in Batangas. The Department of Tourism says demand is coming from leisure, luxury, honeymoon, MICE and destination-wedding segments.

The practical path: visa-free entry and a direct flight

Two policy changes underpin the pitch. Since 8 June 2025, Indian passport holders can visit the Philippines for tourism for up to 14 days without a visa, the Department of Foreign Affairs announced. The stay is non-extendible and non-convertible, and travellers need a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, confirmed accommodation, proof of sufficient funds and a return or onward ticket, according to Marketing-Interactive's report of the DFA announcement.

For longer trips, Indians who hold a valid visa or residence permit from the United States, Japan, Australia, Canada, a Schengen state, Singapore or the United Kingdom — the AJACSSUK group — can enter visa-free for 30 days for tourism. Travellers who need more time, or who are visiting for business, study or work, must use the e-Visa or embassy route instead.

Connectivity has improved in parallel. Air India operates nonstop Delhi-Manila flights five times a week with Airbus A321neo aircraft and is the only carrier offering a direct link between the two countries, with one-stop connections from Europe via Delhi.

What it means for Indian and diaspora travellers

For a diaspora reader planning a Southeast Asia break around a trip home, the arithmetic is now simple: a 14-day Philippines holiday needs no visa appointment at all — book the direct Delhi-Manila flight, keep hotel confirmations and a return ticket within 14 days, and carry proof of funds. Holders of a US, UK, Canadian, Australian, Japanese, Schengen or Singapore visa get 30 days instead, which is enough for a slower Manila-Cebu-Bohol-Boracay circuit.

The awards-night appearance suggests the courtship will continue, with trade events and influencer campaigns aimed at converting interest into bookings. The next test is whether Indian arrivals follow the easier entry rules.
